registered_before: the run starts; no data of it exists
purpose: burden-reduction-v1 rule 5: the <= 3 s choice adopted blind on pulse-stable-confirm (Pulse 5.25) changes the ML stable policy only after one more live run; this is that run

run.name: pulse-peer-discount-confirm
run.policy: sentinel_pulse/protocol/policy-k2of2-a5-peer30.json (sha256 f64c31c0...; joint p, k2of2 alpha x5, evidence discount peer_novelty 30 s)
run.live_implementation: detector/novelty.py + pipeline/peer_exchange.py (port 9479, every worker follows the two others)
run.pairs: 21 workloads x 5 scenarios x 5 rates = 525 attack/control pairs, each with a benign launch (same composition as pulse-stable-confirm)
unchanged_from_pulse_stable_confirm: RCA subscriber (decision-stream trigger, seed, triage labels)

primary_expectations.confirmed_when: all four hold; then policy-k2of2-a5-peer30 becomes the ML stable policy
primary_expectations.if_not_confirmed: the stable policy stays policy-cusum-b3-h6-cap; report the run as is, no re-selection on its data

burden_claim.statistic: normal alert episodes per replica-hour of the live previews (selection start to capture end, campaign excluded), workload bootstrap 95 % CI
burden_claim.claimed_when: live burden <= 0.9 x the burden of each of k2of2 alpha x10 (no discount) and CUSUM b3/h6 cap, both recomputed on this run's window table with the same calibration

implementation_check.statistic: window agreement between the live previews and the offline recomputation of the same rule (burden_blind_test.py --live-rule le3s) on this run's window table
implementation_check.expected: >= 0.999; the only known source of difference is a peer window arriving after the local decision (newest 2 s bucket)
implementation_check.also_reported: peer exchange counters per worker (connects, disconnects, dropped messages), share of windows discounted, live-only / recomputed-only preview windows

reported_without_threshold: recall and p95 per scenario and per rate; rates 1 and 3 per second separately (G4)
RCA coverage, ranking, latency, probe-only share, seed effect, alarm taxonomy
per-replica comparison of the workloads that dominated pulse-stable-confirm (kafka, postgres, inventory; replica_compare.py)
kernel -> recipient latency of the operational alert path
analysis: scripts/after_stable_confirm.sh with RUN=/mnt/sentinel-pulse-archive/pulse-peer-discount-confirm LIVE_RULE=le3s (campaign stage, final stage, compression); replica_compare.py and alert_delivery_latency.py by hand after the run
capture_requirements: experiment output mode (full decisions and features) so every offline replay is possible
decisions carry novel_peer and evidence_discounted; worker STATUS carries the peer exchange counters
Falco logs copied off the nodes during and after the run
no heavy NFS or memory job on any node while the run is active; nothing on masters 2/3
not_claimed: detection of an attack running on every replica of a workload at once (it would be discounted; the campaign attacks one replica)
separation of attacks from benign launches (G5)
attacks entering through an application exploit (recall is an upper bound for attacks entering through exec)
workloads with a single replica gain nothing from the discount
